title: Section 74 ICA — Stipulated sum and reasonable compensation

content.overview: Where a sum is named as payable on breach, or a penalty is stipulated, the claimant is entitled to reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount so named. Indian law does not enforce a pure penalty as such.

sections.heading: Reasonable compensation
sections.body: Section 74 requires reasonable compensation capped by the named sum. Proof of actual loss is the ordinary expectation; difficulty of proof may be relevant in light of Supreme Court guidance (verify reports before citation).

sections.heading: Track B
sections.body: Plead the stipulation, the breach, and facts supporting reasonableness. Expect moderation of extravagant figures. Treat earnest-money forfeiture with separate care under the same provision and case law.

illustrations: A contract states that ₹50,000 is payable on breach. On breach, the court assesses reasonable compensation under section 74, subject to the ₹50,000 ceiling.
